diagram.title: NNX GraphDef and State with shared and copied module identity
diagram.prediction: If `left` and `right` point to the same hidden module, what changes when only one reference is assigned a new bias?
diagram.reading: Read the top row as structure: `GraphDef` records module types, named edges and the shared-reference relation `left is right`. The middle row is the `State` snapshot, with arrays at paths such as `hidden.kernel`, `hidden.bias`, `out.kernel`, `out.bias`, and `calls`. `nnx.merge(GraphDef, State)` rebuilds the object graph. The lower row distinguishes two cases. Reusing the same State variable objects can preserve identity; copying each state leaf before merge gives equal starting values with independent mutable variables. In this lesson the ordinary model has named paths `hidden`, `out`, and `calls`; `left`/`right` are a labelled identity variant of that graph, not extra layers in its parameter-count fixture.
diagram.alt: GraphDef contains module wiring and shared-reference identity, while State contains named arrays for hidden.kernel, hidden.bias, out.kernel, out.bias, and calls. GraphDef plus State enters nnx.merge to reconstruct the model. A shared state reference retains variable identity; copied state leaves reconstruct equal values with independent mutable identity.
